title: Ferdinand, King of Hungary (Ferdinand III) <-> Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand, 1634, 1635, 1640 (DECODE R1887, R1889, R1890; draft R954)

steps.what: DECODE R1887/R1889/R1890 images and transcriptions need authentication; Brussels archive not online. Skipped.
Found https://github.com/aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers with readings of all three letters.
DECODE login cookie: fetched all 8 images of R1887/R1889/R1890, DECODE transcriptions D3605 (R1889) and D3604 (R1890), record pages R953-R955, R1885-R1892.

Schmeh Top 50 #27 / Thomas Ernst 2017 'Zifra Piccolominea' checked: concerns Ferdinand III to Archduke Leopold Wilhelm (20 July 1640 and 1641), not these Brussels letters; Ernst's key does not fit R1889/R1890. research/top50 claim is wrong for this target.
R1890 ciphertext-only homophonic anneal (symbol->letter, la 5-gram + frequency term), 16x4M and 60x10M restarts; control on synthetic 786-token Latin homophonic recovered 99.7%.
R1890 letter groups = their own vowel (pli=i, op=o ...).
Draft R954 (pointed to on the R1889 record): underlined plaintext aligned word by word with R1889's cipher; 74 words, 463 tokens; letter key with 2-5 homophones per letter.
R1890 with R1889 key fixed: free-value anneal of unknown symbols over letters/bigrams/trigrams suggested numbers in vowel series (48=no, 51=re, 53=ro ...).

R1890 family anneal: each letter-group/number family = one consonant + AEIOU vowel; all top restarts converge on the same syllabary (40s=l/n/r+v, pl?=t+v, ?p=c+v, c?=m+v, h?=d+v, t?s=b+v, ?n=s+v, ?u=p+v, m?=f+v, ?t=g+v, g?=h+v).
R1890 completed by context (ko=do, fu=mu, lx=oc, li=xi, 14=tz) and image checks of DECODE's uncertain signs (l/z?=z, c/1?o/0?=co, pla/u?=plu); all 782 tokens assigned; Latin text read in full.
After our recovery, compared with aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers KEY.md and READING-1640.md (18 Sept 2026): same syllabary, same singleton values, same Latin.
R1887 transcribed from the images (no DECODE transcription): 30 lines, 474 tokens, graphic signs labelled.
R1887 family anneal (consonant + shown vowel per letter-group family, rest free): collapsed to bare vowels; with consonants forced, Latin-like but not converged.
R1887 last cipher passage = the following clear words promovere haud dedignetur; fixes 5 families and 11 signs.
R1887 anneal with the crib fixed converges on the remaining families (f?r=c+v, ?c=v+s, p?n=l+v, s?l=b+v, t?s=s+v, l?s=g+v, ?r=f+v) and most signs.
R1887 read word by word with image re-checks (align1887.txt): 88.4% of tokens as sense, 93.9% with conjectures; a 6-token word and a 16-token span before negotium open.
LM span search over value options for the open 16-token R1887 span (span1887.py): fragments only.
R1887 reading compared after the fact with aaymeloglu ferdinand-1634: same families, same open spans; we add suorum and the conjectures ausus quos, eventus, quam ea.
Tomokiyo cryptiana unsolved list: Two of Three Solved (Aymeloglu, 19 Sept 2026). Hildegard Ernst MIOG 100 (1992) on these ciphers not reachable online.

Last attempt on the two open R1887 pieces (crisdus, 16-token span before negotium): every attested value per sign, group vowels fixed, pruned to la-gutenberg word segmentations and ranked by the la LM in context (gap1887.py); crops re-viewed. 571 and 1,704 candidates, none fits the sentence.
research/top50/NOTES.md and README corrected: Ernst 2017 (Top 50 #27) concerns Ferdinand III to Leopold Wilhelm 1640/41, not the Brussels letters.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1244 tokens, 112 types, la order 4: reading -2.023 per letter; random keys -4.505 (z 12.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.969 (mean -3.007, z 31.5); annealer on the real text -2.883. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE and own transcriptions of R1887/R1889/R1890; decryptions copied from NOTES.md to texts/ beside the alignments and literal decode; keys work/key1889.json, key1890_extra.json, key1887.json

Transcription benchmark, letters (research/transcription_benchmark, 19 Nov 2026): three independent blind passes at reading the cipher lines of R1889 and R1890 from page images (rotated 270 degrees clockwise; a first attempt cut at 90 degrees was upside down and was discarded), scored on the lower-cased letter-and-digit stream against DECODE D3605 and D3604 (human, single reference). Error rate R1889 3.7%, 2.9%, 2.9% (684 signs), R1890 2.3%, 3.0%, 2.7% (1,443 signs); vote 2.9% and 2.5%. R1889 page 2 is mostly show-through and only 3 cipher lines were read there.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.993; polyphony 0.009; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.883

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: R1889's alphabet was recovered by aligning it with the draft R954; R1890's syllabary was then recovered from its own ciphertext (family anneal on top of the R1889 alphabet); R1887's repertoire was rebuilt from an in-letter crib (the cipher repeats the following clear words) plus annealing and context.

parts.label: 1635 letter
parts.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
parts.basis: draft R954 aligned word by word; 450/463 tokens (97.2%) give the draft letter, the 13 others copy slips in words the draft fixes

parts.label: 1640 letter
parts.basis: R1889 alphabet fixed, AEIOU-family syllabary annealed with the la model; 782/782 tokens assigned

parts.label: 1634 letter
parts.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
parts.basis: crib from the repeated clear phrase promovere haud dedignetur, crib-seeded family anneal, context; 88.4% of tokens read as sense (93.9% with conjectures); a 6-token word and a 16-token span open after a last dictionary + LM pass

gaps.detail: every sign has a value (45 = s) but the word does not resolve; dictionary + LM pass (gap1887.py) finds no fitting word

gaps.item: R1887 P2.14-15 span before negotium (16 tokens)
gaps.detail: singletons 4) h^ga e~, 4 = m/n/s; LM span search and dictionary + LM pass (span1887.py, gap1887.py) give fragments only

gaps.item: R1887 conjectures ausus quos, eventus, partibus, quam ea
gaps.detail: singleton signs ltu, #, v/, 146, X, c/

gaps.item: R1890 obscured last sign of p.1 line 1

outcome.notes: R1889 and R1890 complete (copy slips igitua, materi, expredse in R1890); R1887 partial. Independent of the Aymeloglu reading except that his README (1640 additions mostly syllables) and SOURCES.md (pointer to R954) were read before the R1889/R1890 work; see conditions.prior_solution.notes. The research/top50 claim that Ernst 2017 solved these letters was wrong and is corrected.

texts.label: R1887, Ferdinand, King of Hungary, to the Cardinal-Infante, Stuttgart, 28 Oct 1634
texts.summary: Written after the victory at Nördlingen: the other side is expected to spare no attempt to restore the princes who put themselves under its protection, above all Württemberg and Durlach, and Ferdinand asks the Cardinal-Infante to oppose the designs of the enemies of the House by a movement and diversion of his arms. A 6-token word and a 16-token span remain open.

texts.label: R1889, the Cardinal-Infante to Ferdinand, King of Hungary, Brussels, 16 Nov 1635
texts.summary: The Cardinal-Infante refuses imperial winter quarters in the archbishopric and city of Trier, which has been under Spanish protection and garrison for two hundred years, and asks that the Spanish garrison keep the town and its surroundings for its own and the Elector's upkeep. Key recovered from the draft R954.

texts.label: R1890, Ferdinand III to the Cardinal-Infante, Vienna, 22 Feb 1640
texts.summary: Ferdinand III answers the new levies of the Elector of Cologne and the Westphalian circle: Count Hatzfeldt is to go to Cologne and raise a larger force, and the Cardinal-Infante is asked again for the hundred thousand florins, to be consigned at Cologne to the imperial commissaries; the Spanish envoy, the marques de Castaneda, will explain further.

prior.where: Andrew Aymeloglu, github.com/aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers: ferdinand-1635-1640 (R1889, R1890 read, 18 Sept 2026) and ferdinand-1634 (R1887 partial, 23 Sept 2026); Tomokiyo's Unsolved list marks them Two of Three Solved. Schmeh Top 50 #27 / Thomas Ernst 2017 concern other letters (Ferdinand III to Leopold Wilhelm). Exposure: Found 30 Sept 2026, not opened. On 9 Oct, after the failed ciphertext-only R1890 run, his README and SOURCES.md were read: the README says the 1640 additions to the 1635 alphabet are mostly syllables; SOURCES.md points to the draft R954 (already on our saved DECODE record of R1889). No key value or reading came from him: KEY.md, the READING files and ferdinand-1634/ were opened only after our recovery, for comparison. The R1890 syllabary recovery was therefore made knowing that the extra symbols are mostly syllables.
